high.title: Oil Prices Break $100 Again - Can Government Keep Inflation in 2% Range in H2?
high.summary: International oil prices have surged sharply amid renewed Middle East tensions, putting significant upward pressure on Korea's inflation outlook for H2 2026. The government's target of maintaining CPI within the 2% range is now under serious threat, with inflation expected to spike to approximately 3% during August–September. A petroleum price shock appears increasingly inevitable, prompting authorities to heighten vigilance and mobilize a full-scale response.

high.title: Why it matters for KRW, bonds, and rates:
USD-KRW Trades in Early 1,460s in New York Session
high.summary:
The USD-KRW exchange rate traded at 1,461.80 won as of 9:18 PM during the New York session on July 24, representing a decline of 5.00 won from the prior session. During regular Seoul trading hours (closing around 3:30 PM), the pair had settled at 1,466.60 won, down only a marginal 0.20 won. The additional KRW strengthening observed in the New York session — roughly 4.80 won beyond the Seoul close — suggests that after-hours USD weakness was the primary driver, likely reflecting broad dollar softness in offshore markets. For KRW traders, the 1,460–1,470 range remains a critical near-term band to monitor. A sustained break below 1,460 could signal further won appreciation, potentially prompting BOK or state-bank smoothing operations. For Korean government bond investors, a firming KRW reduces imported inflation pressure, which could modestly support the case for BOK rate stability or easing. Foreign equity investors should note that KRW strength improves unhedged returns on Korean equity positions. Watch for follow-through in the Seoul open and any BOK commentary on FX volatility.

---

high.title: [FX-Weekly] Won Nears 1,450 Level - Where Are Supply-Demand Dynamics and US-Japan Monetary Policies Headed?
high.summary:
The KRW/USD exchange rate has steadily declined toward the 1,450 won level, driven by persistent dollar-selling flows in the Seoul FX market. This week's key directional drivers will be the monetary policy decisions from both the Federal Reserve (Fed) and the Bank of Japan (BOJ). Market participants are closely watching whether the Fed signals any easing bias — which would further pressure the dollar — and whether the BOJ moves toward additional rate normalization, which could amplify JPY strength and create spillover appreciation pressure on the KRW via the broader Asia FX complex. The dominant supply-demand dynamic currently favors won appreciation, but traders should remain alert to potential reversal risks if the Fed adopts a hawkish hold or if risk sentiment deteriorates. For KRW traders, the 1,450 level represents a technically significant threshold. A sustained break below could open the path toward 1,430–1,420. Bond investors should note that a stronger KRW environment, if accompanied by a dovish Fed signal, could support foreign inflows into Korean government bonds and exert downward pressure on yields.

---

high.title: [Bond Market Weekly] Focus on FOMC Before July Inflation Data
high.summary: Seoul's bond market is expected to remain highly sensitive to external drivers this week, with the July FOMC meeting taking center stage ahead of domestic inflation data. The rate decision will be announced in the early morning hours of July 30 (KST), and bond traders are likely to adopt a cautious, wait-and-see posture until then. With the July CPI print not due until early August, there is limited domestic anchor for bond pricing this week, meaning KTB yields could be disproportionately moved by Fed tone, USD strength, and oil price volatility — all of which are elevated given ongoing Middle East tensions. A hawkish Fed hold or surprise hike would likely steepen selling pressure on KTBs and push USD/KRW higher. Conversely, a dovish hold could provide a modest rally in duration. Fund managers should closely monitor the FOMC statement language and Chair Powell's press conference for any signals on the trajectory of rate cuts, as these will directly impact BOK rate expectations and KRW carry dynamics heading into August.

high.title: [New York FX Market Weekly] Yen at 40-Year Low — BOJ's Dilemma Deepens if Fed Turns Hawkish
high.summary: The New York FX market this week is set to be shaped by the convergence of Middle East geopolitical risk and major central bank decisions from the Fed, Bank of England, and Bank of Japan. Most critically, the Japanese yen has fallen to a 40-year low with USD/JPY approaching 164, as speculative short yen positions have resumed building after a brief pause. The article highlights that even a hawkish Fed hold — without an actual rate hike — could significantly pressure the BOJ by widening the US-Japan rate differential further, deepening the BOJ's policy dilemma. For KRW traders, this dynamic is directly relevant: a weaker yen exerts competitive devaluation pressure on the Korean won, as both currencies often move in tandem during risk-off or dollar-strength episodes. A USD/JPY break above 164 could accelerate USD/KRW upside, potentially drawing BOK attention. Watch also for any BOJ emergency commentary or intervention signals. The FOMC outcome on July 30 will be the pivotal catalyst for both JPY and KRW direction this week.

medium.title: Shinhan Securities Predicts Japan's Long-Term Rates to Peak in Q4 Amid Elevated Yields
medium.summary: Japan's 10-year government bond yields have surged to their highest levels in approximately 30 years, with Shinhan Investment Corp. researchers predicting rates will peak around Q4 2026. The report highlights that near-term resolution of external tightening concerns and uncertainty is necessary before yields stabilize. For Korean markets, persistently elevated JGB yields are directly relevant — they increase the risk-free alternative for regional fixed income investors, exerting indirect upward pressure on KTB yields and weighing on Korean bond valuations. Additionally, yen dynamics driven by BOJ policy normalization can influence USD/KRW through broader Asia FX risk sentiment. Fund managers should track Japan's CPI trajectory and any BOJ forward guidance as a key external risk factor for KTB positioning.

medium.title: South Korea Financial Regulators Release Weekly Schedule
medium.summary: The BOK, Financial Services Commission (FSC), and Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) have released their schedule for the week of July 27–August 1, 2026. Key data releases to monitor include: **Resident Foreign Currency Deposit Trends for June 2026** (Monday, 12:00) — a direct indicator of capital flow and dollarization trends affecting KRW; **Consumer Survey Results for July 2026** (Tuesday, 06:00) — which includes inflation expectations, a key input for BOK policy; and **Financial Institution Weighted Average Interest Rates for June 2026** (Tuesday, 12:00) — providing insight into credit market conditions and lending rate pass-through. The FSC Deputy Governor meeting on Wednesday and Business Survey Index on Thursday round out a data-heavy week that could influence near-term rate and FX expectations. Fund managers should pay particular attention to Monday's FX deposit data and Tuesday's consumer sentiment release.

medium.title: US July S&P PMI – Services Improves, Manufacturing Slows
medium.summary: The preliminary US S&P Global PMI for July showed services activity rising to 53.6 (an eight-month high, up from June's 51.2), while manufacturing slipped to a four-month low of 53.8. The mixed reading complicates the Fed's policy calculus — resilient services inflation could keep the Fed on hold for longer, sustaining USD support and limiting KRW upside. However, the manufacturing softness hints at tariff-related demand headwinds that may weigh on global trade volumes, a key risk for Korea's export-driven economy and current account surplus. Bond investors should monitor whether this data shifts Fed rate cut expectations, as US Treasury yield moves directly influence Korean government bond spreads and foreign capital flows into KRW assets.

medium.title: ECB Chief Economist – Current Situation 'Not a Red Alert' Requiring Swift Action
medium.summary: ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane characterized the current macro environment — including elevated oil prices — as "a medium-sized shock," explicitly distancing it from the emergency easing cycles of 2022. Lane indicated the ECB will assess the appropriate rate level on a meeting-by-meeting basis. A more gradual ECB easing path supports EUR relative to USD at the margin, which could contribute to modest broad-based USD softness — a mild positive for KRW. For Korean bond markets, a less aggressive ECB cutting cycle also reduces pressure on the BOK to front-run global easing, potentially keeping Korean short-end yields better supported.

medium.title: Trump Launches Section 301 Probe Against EU Over Big Tech Fines, Threatens 'Substantial Tariffs'
medium.summary: President Trump threatened substantial tariffs on the EU in retaliation for fines totaling over $20 billion levied against US Big Tech firms including Apple, Meta, and Amazon. An escalating US-EU trade dispute raises global risk-off sentiment, which historically pressures EM currencies including KRW. Additionally, broader tariff escalation fears could dampen global growth expectations, weighing on Korean export volumes and widening the risk premium on KRW assets. Fund managers should treat this as a tail risk to monitor — a full-blown US-EU trade war would likely trigger capital outflows from Korean equities and pressure USD-KRW higher toward the 1,480–1,500 range.

medium.title: Capital Markets Act Amendments and Retail Investor Protections — Governance Reform Watch
medium.summary: Experts are urging legislators to prioritize pending Capital Markets Act amendments over the recently passed Commercial Act revisions as the more effective tool for protecting ordinary shareholders. Unlike the Commercial Act — which focuses on ex-post accountability — the Capital Markets Act contains mechanisms enabling shareholders to receive direct financial compensation or proactively prevent rights violations. The distinction matters for foreign institutional investors monitoring Korea's broader "Corporate Value-Up" reform agenda, as it signals the pace and depth of governance improvement. Progress (or stagnation) on the Capital Markets Act could influence foreign equity inflows into the KOSPI, given that governance discount reduction has been a key thesis for international funds increasing Korean equity exposure. Watch for legislative calendar developments in the National Assembly.

medium.title: National Pension Service Internal Control Probe — Governance & Institutional Flow Risk
medium.summary: A civil coalition has called for a law enforcement investigation into what it describes as a "structural internal control failure" within the National Pension Service's (NPS) investment division, citing allegations of forced investments, abuse of power over external asset managers, and collusion via academic and personal networks. A re-audit has reportedly been ordered. As Korea's largest domestic institutional investor — managing approximately KRW 1,000 trillion in assets — any reputational or operational disruption at the NPS carries implications for domestic equity and bond markets. Funds should monitor whether the probe escalates in a way that disrupts NPS's asset allocation or mandate execution, particularly in Korean government bonds and large-cap KOSPI names where NPS is a dominant holder.

medium.title: Insurance Research Institute Urges Stronger Suitability Checks, Contract Management for Dollar Insurance Sales Amid High Exchange Rates
medium.summary: The Korea Insurance Research Institute has flagged rising consumer risk from the surge in dollar-denominated insurance product sales, driven by the elevated KRW/USD exchange rate environment. Researcher Moon Je-young recommends that insurers strengthen suitability assessments and disclosure practices while monitoring policy surrender and retention trends. From a macro perspective, the growth in dollar insurance uptake by Korean retail investors reflects ongoing demand for USD-denominated assets and could represent a structural source of natural dollar demand that partly offsets won appreciation. Fund managers should note this as a FX flow dynamic to monitor — widespread surrenders or shifts in preference could alter the retail FX demand/supply balance and have modest implications for the KRW.

medium.title: FSS Governor Lee Chan-jin Discusses AI, Supply Chain Response with Asia-Pacific Financial Leaders
medium.summary: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) Governor Lee Chan-jin participated in the 15th EMEAP GHOS meeting, engaging with Asia-Pacific central bank governors and financial supervisory authorities on AI adoption in finance and supply chain disruption risks stemming from global developments. While this is primarily a regulatory and supervisory coordination event, the forum's focus on supply chain risks is relevant given Korea's export-heavy economy and potential trade flow implications for the current account and KRW. International fund managers should monitor any policy signals emerging from EMEAP discussions that could influence regional financial stability frameworks or cross-border capital flow regulations affecting Korea.

medium.title: Trump Halts Iran Strikes — Can US and Iran Find Common Ground on Strait of Hormuz?
medium.summary: The US has halted airstrikes on Iran for the first time after nearly two weeks of continuous military operations, prompting speculation about a potential diplomatic opening over the Strait of Hormuz standoff. It remains uncertain whether this pause is a tactical breather ahead of renewed strikes or a genuine de-escalation. For Korean markets, this is a medium-term risk factor: any re-escalation threatening Hormuz passage would spike global oil prices, worsening Korea's import bill, widening the trade deficit, and applying depreciation pressure on KRW. A sustained de-escalation, conversely, would be a modest positive for KRW and Korean equities. Traders should monitor Strait of Hormuz shipping flow data and oil price reactions as leading indicators.

medium.title: CNN Reports US Vice President, Joint Chiefs Chairman Raised Escalation Concerns With Trump
medium.summary: CNN reports, citing a Pentagon source, that operations against Iran are "currently on hold," with Iranian military confirming the US has halted attacks for two days and that Iran has also suspended retaliation. Senior US officials including the Vice President and Joint Chiefs Chairman reportedly raised concerns with Trump about escalation risks. While this points toward a de-escalatory impulse within the US administration, the situation remains fluid. For KRW and KTB markets, reduced geopolitical risk premium is modestly supportive, but the key watchpoint remains whether a diplomatic channel can be established — or whether hostilities resume, reigniting oil price and safe-haven USD demand pressures on EM Asian currencies including KRW.
